Office styling and layout

knittogether works by converting Office documents → markdown → Quarto → Office.
To keep formatting consistent throughout this round‑trip, it’s important to structure and style your Word and PowerPoint files correctly.

This guide covers:

  • How Word styles translate to markdown
  • Using reference .docx and .pptx templates
  • Managing captions, headings, lists, and layout
  • Creating hidden placeholder styles
  • Avoiding Word formatting that Pandoc cannot interpret
  • Ensuring PowerPoint output respects your template
  • Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

Word Styling

Word documents are best treated as structured, not manually formatted, documents. Pandoc relies heavily on Word’s built‑in styles to produce correct markdown.

Ensure all content uses Word’s official styles such as Title Heading 1-6, Normal, List Paragraph, and Caption.

Pandoc ignores or flattens items such as text boxes, SmartArt, WordArt, and shapes containing text. Converting these to text format or saving as an image with appropriate caption allows them to be rendered as desired.

Tables with long text or line breaks may need adjustment to the Pandoc conversion process as described in vignette("extended-workflow"). Merged cells in tables should be avoided.

Avoid manually changing font, size, alignment, or colour on individual paragraphs. Instead, modify the style itself (Home → Styles → Modify). This is because pandoc converts these into markdown as follows:

Word style Markdown output
Heading 1 #
Heading 2 ##
Heading 3 ###
Caption Markdown figure/table caption syntax
Normal Plain paragraphs
List Paragraph - / 1. lists

Captions (images & tables)

Word captions must be inserted via Word’s built‑in tool: Right‑click image/table → Insert Caption

This ensures Pandoc recognises the caption as:

  • an image/table
  • with a formal caption
  • with a stable anchor to the media file

Avoid typing captions manually below images as they will not be detected.

Reference documents

Quarto lets you specify a custom Word or PowerPoint template:

format:
  docx:
    reference-doc: reference.docx

Word

Your reference document should define the Styles supported by pandoc markdown such as Headers 1-6, body text and lists. It is advisable to take a blank Word file, ideally one generated via Quarto/pandoc and:

  • Modify only the Styles, not the body text
  • Save as reference.docx
  • Store it in your project or shared template folder
  • Reference it from your .qmd

To prevent formatting outside of supported and tested style from being used. This can be achieved by going through Review → Protect → Restrict Editing.

PowerPoint

PowerPoint styling is controlled via a template (.pptx) master slide deck. Pandoc supports a limited set of slide layouts.

Advanced features

Callouts and other components

While not ideal for readability in Word, it is possible to specify components such as callouts by adding the syntax directly in the document. For instance, this will render a callout when read into Quarto.

This is a word document.

::: {.callout-warning}
# Warning!
This is a callout warning.
:::

Making placeholders less disruptive

For the ease of reading, placeholders are wrapped in a custom styling. If Word or HTML documents have the relevant styling, placeholders can be hidden from view. In Word this can be toggled with the ¶ button on the Home tab or with CTRL + *. Consideration should be made to whether this makes it easier or harder for users editing the Word document as invisible content is easier to accidentally delete.

An example Word document is provided in this package and is accessible via system.file("extdata", "PlaceholderMarker_example.docx", package = "knittogether"). To apply the style to an arbitrary Word document, create a custom character style with the Hidden font attribute enabled. In Word: Home → Styles → New Style → Style type: Character → Format → Font → tick Hidden. Reveal placeholders by toggling Show/Hide (¶).
